title: Oncall Rhythm & SLO Sprint Notes — Apr 12 2027
content:
Context
Week snapshot for the oncall rotation covering Apr 5–12. Purpose: capture recurring patterns in alerts, current SLO tilt, and immediate operational actions. Notes here are intentionally conversational — use for handoffs, follow-up, and decisions for next sprint.

Highlights / TL;DR
- SLO status: read SLOs for hosted text-generation are green for availability (99.97%), but latency SLO for p95 slipped from target 200ms to ~420ms during one 36m window on Apr 7.
- Root cause candidate: sudden KV cache thrash after model routing rule change + noisy long-context requests from a single customer pool.
- Secondary issue: an autoscaler misconfiguration caused delayed pod scale-up for dedicated pools (affects Dedicated-us-west-2). Scaling target threshold was set to 70% cpu (should be 55%) in last week's hotfix.
- Action items created and owners assigned below; priority on stabilizing prefix caching and tightening autoscale thresholds.

Standup summaries (by day)
Mon 2027-04-05
- Morning standup: low alert volume. Investigated higher token churn on small fraction of requests.
- Tasks: Diego to trace KV eviction logs; Priya to audit recent routing rule changes.

Tue 2027-04-06
- Oncall noticed increased tail latency for model-5b when sequence length > 2048. Temporary mitigation: apply per-request sequence cap at 2048 in the routing gateway for a 4-hour window.
- Note: this cap has product implications — flagged to Solutions-eng.

Wed 2027-04-07 (Incident window)
- 10:42 UTC: P95 latency spikes observed (from 180ms -> 420ms). Error rate remained low.
- 10:44: Pager alert routed to SRE oncall (Owen).
- 10:50: Correlated with a routing config rollout (rollout-id: route-2027-04-07-01) that added a new weight to model-5b-long for a customer experiment.
- 11:02: Observed KV cache churn: cache hit ratio for model-5b dropped from 0.91 -> 0.22 in 12 minutes.
- 11:10: Rollback of routing change initiated; hit ratio recovered to 0.85 by 11:24. P95 back to ~190ms by 11:30.
- Post-incident notes: no data loss, no customer-facing errors, but latency SLO breach window recorded.

Thu 2027-04-08
- Postmortem kickoff. Diego started collection of perf snapshots + heatmaps. Priya drafting primer on safe rollout steps for routing weight changes.
- Began prototype for per-customer KV quotas to prevent noisy tenants from thrashing shared caches.

Fri 2027-04-09
- Dedicated autoscaler behavior observed: slow-to-scale for burst traffic in dedicated pools. Found misapplied threshold in k8s HorizontalPodAutoscaler (HPA) for dedicated-gpu-pool-2.
- Change made: set target CPU to 55% (was 70%). Followed up with stress test.

Sat/Sun 2027-04-10-11
- Low activity. Oncall rotated without major incidents. Quick noisy-tenant alert on Sun morning resolved by soft rate-limiting rule.

Monday Handoff (Apr 12) notes
- Incidents: route-rollout-induced KV thrash (see incident log). SRE oncall to monitor p95 and cache hit ratio dashboards for next 7 days.
- Open tickets to monitor: JIRA-OPS-1982 (investigate cache isolation), JIRA-OPS-1991 (autoscaler tuning for dedicated pools).
- Immediate mitigations: rollback + temporary per-request sequence cap.
- Longer-term: implement tenant-level KV quotas, add canary check for routing changes that simulates cache access pattern, automated rollback on cache-hit-ratio drop.

Incident timeline (compact)
- 10:42 UTC: p95 alert triggers (p95 exceeded 400ms for 5 consecutive minutes)
- 10:44 UTC: pager to Owen Park
- 10:50 UTC: initial hypothesis formed (routing change coincident)
- 11:02 UTC: cache-hit metric drops -> confirm thrash
- 11:10 UTC: rollback started
- 11:24 UTC: cache-hit ratio trending back up
- 11:30 UTC: p95 within SLO target

SLO snapshot (this week)
- Availability SLO (hosted read/stream endpoints): target 99.95% -> measured 99.97%
- Latency SLO (p95 gen): target 200ms -> 7-day rolling average 210ms but spike on Apr 7 hit 420ms for 36m window (SLO minor breach recorded)
- Error rate SLO: target <0.1% -> measured 0.04%
- Notes: trending latency drift tied to longer context churn; need to test KV eviction policies under mixed workloads.

Remediation & action items (with owners)
- Implement tenant-level KV quotas (Diego A.) — design doc due Apr 19; milestone: initial rate limiter in staging by Apr 26.
- Canary gating for routing weight changes (Priya K.) — add pre-rollout check that runs a synthetic cache-access pattern; PR #3142 in review.
- Autoscaler audit (Owen P.) — audit HPAs for dedicated pools, create baseline runbook for threshold settings; complete by Apr 18.
- Post-incident retro + playbook update (Maya C.) — capture checklist for rolling back routing changes and add runbook link to oncall deck.
- SLO alert tuning (SRE team) — reduce p95 alert threshold margin to detect early drift, avoid noisy flapping.

Notes to self / open questions
- How do we safely test tenant-level quotas in staging without modelling 1,000s of tenant patterns? Synthetic tenant generator?
- Can we add a lightweight simulation step to the CI for routing changes that exercises cache locality? Perf overhead will be small if we limit to a rollout canary.
- Consider a dedicated small cache shard per heavy tenant (cost vs complexity trade-off).

Hand-off checklist for next oncall
- Watch dashboards: p95-gen-main, cache-hit-ratio (model-5b), dedicated-gpu-pool-2 CPU utilization
- Keep an eye on JIRA-OPS-1982 and PR #3142 status
- If p95 > 300ms for >10m, escalate to pager and start rollback protocol (runbook section 3.2)
- For autoscale lag: manually trigger scale-test job in staging and compare HPA events to production timeline

Appendix: quick logs + evidence pointers
- Perf snapshots folder: /shared/perf-snapshots/2027-04-07-model-5b
- Heap of KV eviction logs: S3://redwood-ops/logs/kv-evictions/2027-04-07/
- Slack thread: #ops-incident-2027-04-07 (link above in metadata)

Draft decisions for product review (need alignment)
- Short-term: keep sequence cap at 2048 for model-5b-long traffic for 72 hours while we prototype tenant quotas.
- Mid-term: implement canary gating for routing changes; require at least 60m green canary on cache metrics before ramp to 100%.
- Long-term: consider per-tenant cache isolation for top 50 tenants or apply dynamic cache quotas.

Closing thoughts
- This event feels like a classic noisy-tenant on shared cache problem. We have enough telemetry to drive a focused mitigation path (quotas + canary checks). The autoscaler misconfig is lower-severity but should be a quick win and reduce future latency exposure.
- Please add any missing context or links below and flag blockers in the JIRA tickets.

----
End of oncall rhythm notes (Maya Chen)
